headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill shifts certain electricity costs, including capacity procurement and distribution infrastructure, onto high-load users like data centers, aiming to reduce residential ratepayers' bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Senator Louise Lucas, Delegate Destiny LeVere Bolling, Dominion Energy (initially, for original goals).
opponents: Large energy users, data center industry (due to increased costs).
news_headline: Governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers. Critics say her tweaks weaken them.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393, a key energy measure designed to shift more costs onto data centers and large manufacturers to save residential electricity customers money and expand a power line burial program. Critics, including Dominion Energy, argue that the Governor's amendments undermine the original goals of lowering costs for customers and reducing outages.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities to report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water provided to data centers monthly, enhancing transparency on water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (potential administrative burden, though some utilities indicate it's manageable).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public.
news_summary: A new Virginia law, identical to SB 553, mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage, which will be made publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide transparency on the industry's water consumption, though some utilities anticipate minimal impact on existing services or budgets.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires data center applicants to conduct site assessments for sound profiles near residential areas and schools, and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites before approval.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data centers, environmental groups, Delegate Thomas.
opponents: Data center industry, developers (due to potential restrictions and additional assessment requirements).
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Pass 15 Data Center Bills as Tax Exemption Fight Looms.
news_summary: Virginia lawmakers passed several data center bills in 2026, including HB 153, which introduces new siting requirements for large data centers. This bill mandates impact assessments on sound profiles near homes and schools, and allows localities to require assessments of impacts on water resources, agriculture, and historic sites before rezoning approval.
